errorCodes.meaning: The token names no invite this relying party holds, or one already redeemed.
The invite's lifetime has elapsed. Ask the administrator for a new one.
Five wrong claim codes were presented for this invite, and it has been voided — by this request or an earlier one. Ask the administrator for a new one.
The document is not signed by the subject the invite was issued for. Checked before the claim code, and not counted as a wrong code.
The claim code is wrong. `details.attemptsRemaining` MAY state how many wrong codes remain before the invite is voided.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Response.description: The enrolment ceremony the invite authorises: what the approver's enrolment statement is to be made over.

audience.description: The relying party's DID, which the statement names as its `audience` and `recipient`.

challenge.description: A fresh challenge (≥128 bits) the approver signs over in its auth/step-up/approver/attest/0.1 statement with `purpose: enrol`.

enrollmentId.description: Opaque, single-use handle for this ceremony. Echoed in redeem/finish, and the `boundTo` of the approver's enrolment statement.

expiresAt.description: When this ceremony lapses (not the invite). No later than the invite's own expiry.

schema.description: The invited subject, signing as their own DID, presents an auth/step-up/approver/invite token and its claim code, and the relying party opens an enrolment ceremony with a challenge for the approver to sign. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

claimCode.description: The claim code the administrator delivered separately. Never logged; compared with its stored hash.

token.description: The invite token, as carried in the invite URL.
